about: One loudness target for every Play app (docs/research/12-band-sound.md §11). The band goes through make-up gain and then the soft limiter; the original recording (and any rendered clip played as the band) is measured once, as a whole, and gained to the loudness the band plays that arrangement at (recording.band_estimate); the metronome click peaks at metronome.click_peak_dbfs. sounds/playback_levels.py --vectors writes sounds/output-stage-vectors.json from this file.

limiter.about: Memoryless soft limiter: y = x for |x| <= threshold, else sign(x) * (threshold + (ceiling - threshold) * tanh((|x| - threshold) / (ceiling - threshold))). No attack or release, so it cannot pump, and below the threshold every part keeps its level.

band.about: Calibration: the full-band test phrase (sounds/phrases.py, phrases.json 'band') played through each app's band path lands at phrase_lufs within tolerance_lu, peaking at or below the ceiling. gain_db is each path's make-up gain before the limiter, measured, because the synths leave the band at different levels. Every app plays the score's dynamics (see dynamics), so a whole arrangement lands at the same level everywhere: arrangement_lufs is the Mikkel golden score on Windows (alphaSynth, sounds-2026.09.30 pack), measured once alphaTab played its ties as written (before, notes held into the next phrase made it -10.99). Apple plays it at -11.99 with the hall, 2.45 LU louder: its brass matches (stems summed without percussion: -26.71 against -26.90), the kit plays 4.8 dB hot (hi-hats and cymbals: AVAudioUnitSampler hardly applies the kit's zone attenuation) and the hall adds 1.2 LU over the dry band on this sparse score.

dry_room_gain_db.about: Apple only: added to the make-up gain when "Concert hall sound" is off, so the band keeps its loudness without the hall. The hall's share of the band's loudness, measured on the golden arrangement and the Old Hundredth fixture (hall minus room).

apple_seat_trim_db.about: Apple only: added to each part's channel gain by its seat (mapping.json parts[].seat). The environment node places every part at its seat (HRTF, distance), which changes the balance against alphaSynth, which plays every part centred: measured with each part of the full-band phrase alone at velocity 80, hall off, relative to the Solo Cornet (DynamicsLevelTests.partBalance against RenderHarnessTests.Measure_part_balance). The trims bring every part within 1 dB of alphaSynth's balance.

dynamics.about: Score dynamics to MIDI velocity, alphaTab 1.8.4's rules (MusicXmlImporter, MidiFileGenerator._getNoteVelocity, MidiUtils.dynamicToVelocity), which Android and Windows get from alphaTab itself and Apple (ScoreKit Dynamics) copies. A <dynamics> mark, in a direction or in a note's notations, holds from where it is read until the next one, in document order; a part starts at default. velocity is each mark's velocity by MusicXML element name. The forced marks (sf, sfz, fz, sfp) play as ff and hold like any mark, as alphaTab plays them. accent_steps: an <accent/> adds one step (step velocity), a <strong-accent/> (marcato) two; the result is clamped to 1..127. <sound dynamics> is ignored.
dynamics.wedge: Apple only: a hairpin (<wedge>) moves the velocity linearly in time from the mark in effect where it starts to the first mark at or up to a bar after where it stops; with no such mark, one step up or down, held until the next mark. alphaTab 1.8.4 draws hairpins but does not play them, so on Android and Windows the level jumps at the next mark instead.

sampler_velocity.about: Per-synth velocity correction: [score velocity, velocity sent to the synth] knots, linear between them. alphaSynth plays amplitude proportional to velocity and is the reference (no correction). AVAudioUnitSampler ignores the SoundFont's velocity modulator and follows a much steeper curve, so the table's pp played 7 dB softer and ff 3.4 dB louder than on alphaSynth. Measured with the full-band test phrase at one velocity through both engines, 12 dB under the calibrated gain so nothing reaches the limiter, with the same SoundFont (brasscribe-band-16bit.sf2): pitched parts are matched level for level; percussion, which Apple seats further back (about 8 dB under alphaSynth at every velocity), is matched in shape, anchored at velocity 90. alphatab_lufs is the reference: the pitched parts of that phrase through alphaSynth at each velocity. With the correction every table velocity from ppp to fff lands within 1 dB of it except p (-2.5 dB, where the sampler's velocity layers leave a 5 dB gap between 55 and 56).

recording.about: The original recording plays at the loudness the band plays the arrangement at: target = clamp(band_estimate(arrangement), min_target_lufs, max_target_lufs), or fallback_lufs when there is no arrangement or it has no pitched note. The recording is measured once, as a whole (EBU R128 integrated, whole file, a mono file measured as dual mono because it plays from both speakers). gain = clamp(target - measured, -max_cut_db, max_boost_db); 0 when the file is silent. The limiter follows the gain, so a boost cannot clip.

band_estimate.about: Estimated integrated LUFS of the band playing an arrangement, from its dynamics and how many parts sound at once: estimate = offset_db + 10*log10(sum over notes of d * 10^(L(v)/10) / U). The notes: every pitched note of every part (percussion parts are left out; each note of a chord counts, grace notes do not), d its length in quarter notes of score time (tempo is not read), v the velocity it plays at by the dynamics rules (the mark in effect plus accents, before any per-synth velocity correction). L(v): dynamics.sampler_velocity.alphatab_lufs, linear between its knots, L(lowest) + 20*log10(v/lowest) below the lowest knot, L(highest) above the highest. U: the length of score time in which at least one pitched note sounds. More parts sounding at once, or louder marks, raise the estimate by the energy they add. offset_db is fitted on two arrangements measured with their dynamics on Windows (sounds-2026.09.30 pack): the Mikkel golden (-14.44 LUFS, estimate -14.60) and Old Hundredth (-15.68, estimate -15.53). The full-band phrase, a synthetic tutti, plays louder than the estimate says (band.phrase_lufs -12.0, estimate -15.42).

metronome.about: The click's peak after the output, whatever path it takes: about 9 dB under the full band's peak, below the limiter's threshold. gain_db is each path's click volume, measured: Apple's click bypasses the band stage, Android's and Windows' go through it.
